articles.title: 2 men charged in break-in at country residence of Prince William, Princess of Wales
articles.summary: British police said Tuesday that two men have been arrested over a suspected burglary at the Royal Family's Sandringham Estate. It follows reports that the home of Prince William and Princess…

image.caption: A police officer is shown Monday after a burglary was reported at Anmer Hall, a property on the Sandringham Estate belonging to the Prince and Princess of Wales, often used as a country retreat for the family. (Martin Pope/Getty Images)

blocks.text: World·New

British police said Tuesday that two men have been arrested over a suspected burglary at the Royal Family's Sandringham Estate. It follows reports that the home of Prince William and Princess Catherine on the vast royal estate was broken into on Monday.
Charges include trespassing, entering a dwelling with intent to steal
Two men have been charged with burglary at the country home of Prince William and Princess Catherine, police said Wednesday.

The Norfolk Police force said Mirgen Doku, 34, and Arilen Ndoci, 32, were charged with entering a dwelling with intent to steal and trespassing on a protected site. They are due in court later Wednesday.

Police officers were called Monday evening to reported "suspicious activity" at an address on the royal family's rural Sandringham estate in eastern England. After a search involving police dogs, drones and a helicopter, two men were arrested on suspicion of burglary and trespassing.
No members of the Royal Family were on the property at the time.
William and Kate's Kensington Palace office declined to comment on security matters.
Anmer Hall, a 10-bedroom house on the Sandringham estate, was a wedding present to the couple from the late Queen Elizabeth.

William and Kate use the secluded red brick Georgian mansion about 171 kilometres north of London as a country residence on weekends. The couple and their three children spend most of their time at Forest Lodge in Windsor, west of London, which they have described as their "forever home."
Intruders have breached royal properties several times over the years.

Britain's Prince William and Catherine, Princess of Wales, are shown in Mumbai on Nov. 17. The couple are now back in Britain, but were not at their country residence Monday when a break-in occurred. (Rafiq Maqbool/The Associated Press)

In October 2024, burglars broke into the Windsor Castle estate west of London and stole a pickup truck and a quad bike from a farm building. Charles and Queen Camilla weren't at Windsor Castle at the time, but it was reported that William and Kate were in their nearby house.

Three years earlier, a man armed with a crossbow was detained on the castle grounds. Jaswant Singh Chail was later sentenced to nine years in prison after admitting he had been encouraged by a chatbot to kill Elizabeth.

In 1982, intruder Michael Fagan managed to sneak into the queen's private chambers while she was in bed. The queen spent 10 minutes chatting with the burglar before raising the alarm when he asked for a cigarette.

items: When Aline Chrétien discovered an intruder at 24 Sussex Drive

blocks.text: As well, there was a security incident earlier this year at Sandringham when Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, the former prince, was allegedly threatened by a masked man while walking his dogs.

A court case for the 39-year-old man who was charged in connection with the incident is ongoing. Andrew, who was stripped of his royal titles and removed from his longtime Windsor Castle residence, now lives at Marsh Farms on the Sandringham estate..
With files from CBC News

articles.title: DOJ vows to fast-track release of eligible PDLs aged 70 and up
articles.summary: The Department of Justice (DOJ) on Wednesday committed to expedite the release of eligible persons deprived of liberty (PDLs) aged 70 and above as part of efforts to decongest jails.

blocks.text: Published November 25, 2026 6:51pm
The Department of Justice (DOJ) on Wednesday committed to expedite the release of eligible persons deprived of liberty (PDLs) aged 70 and above as part of efforts to decongest jails.
Budget sponsor Senator Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan said this during the Senate plenary deliberations into the proposed P44.283 billion budget of the DOJ and its attached agencies for fiscal year 2027.

“According to the good Secretary, this December 7, the Executive — Office of the President through the Deputy Executive Secretary for Legal Affairs — will be precisely discussing how to fast-track the procedure and to discuss those pending matters for release with the OP,” Pangilinan said.
This came after Senator Imee Marcos appealed to fast-track the release of PDLs who are already very old and have served their sentences for many years.
Eligibility

“Pakiusap na lamang ito na palayain ang mga lola. Dahil alam naman natin kapag 'yung PDL ay 70 years old or older and has served 10 years, 22 years, 'yung iba sa kanila higit pa, they are primarily eligible for executive clemency, hindi na regular parole,” Marcos said.

(Please just release the elderly PDLs. We know that when the PDL is 70 years old or older and has served 10 years, 22 years, some of them even more, they are primarily eligible for executive clemency, not regular parole.)

“We are all very clear that the age and the time served, the high risk status which is no longer extant even if they were convicted of a heinous crime, at that advanced age they are absolutely no threat to society,” she added.

Marcos cited Malacañang’s Memorandum Order No. 155, directing the Bureau of Corrections (BuCor), Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP), and the Board of Pardons and Parole (BPP) to immediately forward to the Office of the President records of inmates who are 70 years and above and are serving sentence by final judgment in order that the same may be considered for the purpose of extending executive clemency.

The agencies were also ordered to automatically submit names of inmates turning 70 years old and to transmit records of the said inmates to the Office of the President for review of their eligibility for executive clemency.
The senator also said the elderly PDLs could avail of the good conduct time allowance under the under Republic Act No. 10592.
Holidays

“Sana habulin na natin. December na po, Pasko na. Panahon na talaga para sa executive clemency. 'Yun lang ang hinihiling ko kasi kung tutuusin, lumalabag rin tayo sa batas sa kaka-delay nang kaka-delay,” Marcos said.

(I hope we can catch up now. It’s already December, it’s Christmas soon. It really is time for executive clemency. That is all I am asking for, because, honestly, we are actually violating the law ourselves by constantly delaying this.)

“They are really qualified and deserving. Marami sa kanila may (many of them have) terminal cancer and other illnesses — they are already wheelchair-bound, and they have families and institutions perfectly happy to take care of them,” she continued.
Citing data from DOJ, Pangilinan said the number of PDLs being released has increased since 2020.
“In 2024, halos 100% ang dumoble na ang mga releases from 2020. In 2025, about, from 57,000, they released 75,000---that's about 50% more,” the budget sponsor said.
(In 2024, the releases reached almost 100%, double the figures from 2020. In 2025, from 57,000, they released 75,000---that's about 50% more.)
“So dumadami na ang number of PDLs being released (so the number of PDLs being released is increasing). The rate has increased, but yes, they still need to do it faster,” he added. — BAP, GMA News

articles.title: Australia, Solomon Islands sign sweeping pact seen as countering China
articles.summary: Australia will become the Solomon Islands' primary security partner, while the archipelago will reject any foreign power trying to "interfere" on its "sensitive" infrastructure.

image.caption: The deal is another win for Australia, which is competing with China for influence in the regionImage: Lukas Coch/AAP/IMAGO

blocks.text: Australia and the Solomon Islands signed a security pact on Wednesday that makes Australia the archipelago's main defense partner.
This came four years after the Pacific islands country signed a similar deal with China.
The deal ‌is a win ⁠for ⁠Canberra, which is battling China for influence in the region. It also recently secured similar agreements with Papua New Guinea, Vanuatu and Fiji.
With the deal, Australia will support the expansion and development of the Solomon Islands' law enforcement.

It also includes Australian funding for investment in infrastructure and education, improved visa arrangements for Solomon Islanders, and requires ‌Honiara to consult Australia on the development of critical infrastructure.
Solomon Islands' "sensitive" infrastructure will also "remain free from militarization, foreign interference and unauthorized access".

This covers airports, ports, energy and telecommunications infrastructure, sectors where China has invested through million-dollar loans since the Solomon Islands switched diplomatic ties from Taiwan to Beijing in 2019.
How Pacific islands beat the China-Australia power struggle

"Australia is proud to be the Solomon Islands' main security partner, and that's a ​responsibility that ‌we take seriously," Prime Minister Anthony Albanese told a joint press conference in Australian capital Canberra with his Solomon Islands counterpart, Matthew Wale.

Albanese also said the Solomon Islands would also be required to consult with Australia before striking deals with non-Pacific Island Forum countries on critical infrastructure or security cooperation.
"Solomon Islands has been for a number of years a source of uncertainty and doubt in the region. Those days are done," Wale told the press conference.
Will the China deal be affected?

Wale has been rebuilding diplomatic relationships with Canberra and Washington since he was elected in May. His predecessor Manasseh Sogavare had built closer ties with China since coming to power in 2019.

Asked whether he had ended the 2022 security pact with Beijing, Wale told journalists that he could not comment due to a non-disclosure clause in the treaty with China, set to expire in April 2027. Discussions with China were "ongoing," he said.
Taiwan minister to DW: 'You cannot be naive' with China

Asked the same question on Wednesday, China's Foreign Ministry did not confirm whether the deal had been scrapped, news agency AFP reported. However, ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun warned Australia and the Solomon Islands that their cooperation "should not target any third party."

“I think this deal, coupled with indications that the Solomon Islands will allow its agreement with China to lapse, goes beyond the success of previous deals Australia has struck in the region,” Connor Graham, a research fellow in the Pacific Islands Program at the Sydney-based Lowy Institute, told Reuters news agency.
He said it was a "blow to Chinese security ambitions in the Pacific."

articles.title: Pope Leo calls COP31 failure ‘troubling,’ urges action on climate change
articles.summary: 'This situation calls for a renewed sense of shared responsibility, new forms of solidarity among nations and fundamental changes in behaviors, socio-economic systems, and the governance of our…

blocks.text: Pope Leo gestures from the popemobile during the weekly general audience in St. Peter's Square at the Vatican, November 25, 2026.
Remo Casilli/Reuters

'This situation calls for a renewed sense of shared responsibility, new forms of solidarity among nations and fundamental changes in behaviors, socio-economic systems, and the governance of our societies,' says the Pope

VATICAN CITY – Pope Leo XIV on Wednesday, November 25, sharply criticized the failure of UN climate talks over the weekend, calling the outcome “troubling” and urging world leaders to step up efforts to combat climate change.

“In the face of the growing frequency of extreme environmental events linked to the climate crisis, it is troubling that COP31 ended without the international community adopting clear commitments to address it seriously and responsibly,” the pope told pilgrims at his weekly audience in St. Peter’s Square.

“This situation calls for a renewed sense of shared responsibility, new forms of solidarity among nations and fundamental changes in behaviors, socio-economic systems, and the governance of our societies,” said the Pope.

The COP31 talks collapsed on Sunday, November 22, as the European Union and others rejected a final deal put forward by COP31 presidents Turkey and Australia, saying it was too weak to advance the fight against global warming.
The last time UN climate talks failed to get a deal adopted was after a summit in Copenhagen in 2009.
Leo is known for speaking carefully in public and makes appeals to the international community in his weekly audiences on a less frequent basis than his predecessor, Pope Francis.

Leo, the first US-born pope, has urged the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics to protect the Earth. Last year, he approved a new Catholic rite of Mass that exhorts people to care for creation, in a first for the global Church. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Fact check: Deepfakes and 'US abandons Taiwan' claims spread ahead of vote
articles.summary: Ahead of local elections, AI-generated falsehoods targeting Democratic Progressive Party mayoral candidate Puma Shen have surged in Taiwan, alongside disinformation claiming the US is pulling back…

image.caption: DPP supporters at a campaign event ahead of Taiwan's local elections, which have seen a rise in online disinformationImage: Cheng Yu-chen/AFP

blocks.text: On November 28, Taiwan will hold local elections that could reshape power dynamics between the sovereignty-leaning Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) and the Beijing-friendly Kuomintang (KMT). The outcome could influence relations between Taiwan and China, as well as regional geopolitics and ties between Washington, Beijing and Taipei.

A month before the election, there was a spike in AI-generated content featuring DPP Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen. Claims that the US is abandoning Taiwan also increased during the same period. Experts say that fake quotes and misleading clips are being used as part of a campaign to weaken trust in US security commitments.
Did Trump offer to sell US arms to China?

Research by DW Fact check found that identical disinformation headlines claiming US troops were withdrawing from Taiwan repeatedly appeared as both articles and videos on Chinese clickbait platforms NetEase and Sohu. The V-Dem Institute at the University of Gothenburg ranked Taiwan "the country most severely targeted" by foreign disinformation for eleven consecutive years – from 2014 to 2024.

The Taiwanese Ministry of the Interior has stated that foreign actors are increasingly using diverse methods to interfere in elections. That includes manipulating election betting, inviting Taiwanese citizens to China, using donations from Taiwanese business people to organize events, such as banquets, and leveraging temple and religious activities, to mobilize and win over supporters. Taiwan has functioned with de facto independence since 1949 despite Beijing's decadeslong claim to the island as a province and repeated vows to annex it.
DW Fact Check examined viral claims that have circulated online since September during the run-up to the election.
Deepfake audio, video target pro-sovereignty candidate
Claim: Puma Shen takes drug and receives kickbacks through arms purchases from the US.
DW Fact check: Fake

blocks.caption: AI-generated audio recordings attacking DPP's Taipei mayoral candidate circulated on Facebook one month before Taiwan's local electionsImage: Facebook

blocks.text: An audio clipposted on Facebook on October 29, claims to show Puma Shen, the DPP candidate for Taipei mayor, admitting to receiving kickbacks from US arms deals.

The recording is heavy with background noise – a method used mask synthetic manipulation in AI-generated audio. Multiple deepfake detection platforms, including Is this AI and Undetectable, flagged the audio as likely AI-generated.

The Facebook account that posted the audio was created on October 29, 2026 – the date the audio was also published. The account's followers are mainly profiles using languages, such as English, Arabic and Thai. That points to possible bot activity.
Another Facebook accountposted an image of Puma Shen taking drugs. Apart from the "AI content" label on the post, multiple AI detector tools identified this photo as likely AI-generated.

blocks.caption: Taiwanese independent media platform Watchout discovered that the advertiser behind this Facebook account is located in ChinaImage: Facebook

blocks.text: The account was created in March 2026. Since then, a lot of AI-generated content mocking Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te and his pro-sovereignty party has been posted. It is occasionally interspersed with posts praising the development of Chinese cities.
This account's profile indicates that the primary country location for people who manage this page includes China and Taiwan.

Taiwanese independent media platform Watchoutinvestigated the account's advertising activity and found that it had previously run at least five Facebook ads. The advertisers were identified as Peng Zhiwei and Guo Yang, both based in China. The findings suggest that the account received financial support from individuals in China.

blocks.caption: The AI detection tool "AI or Not" indicates that this photo is likely AI-generatedImage: aiornot.com

blocks.text: The Taipei mayoral race is a key battleground in Taiwan's upcoming local elections. As of mid-November, polls showed a neck-and-neck contest between Puma Shen and his opponent, Chiang Wan-an, who claims to be a great-grandson of Taiwanese leader Chiang Kai-shek.
Chiang Kai-shek was a leading figure of the Kuomintang and relocated with the party to Taiwan in 1949 after losing the Chinese Civil War to the Chinese Communist Party.

While the Kuomintang was historically staunchly anti-communist, critics argue that it now promotes closer ties with China. For example, they point to senior Kuomintang figure's proposed 10-year unification framework as evidence that its stance runs counter to mainstream public opinion in Taiwan. Although Kuomintang subsequently stated that this framework is entirely unrelated to the current party leadership, it has sparked controversy in Taiwan.
Sensational headlines on Chinese platform
Claim: 500 US troops urgently withdrawn from Taiwan.
DW Fact check: Misleading
A post in Simplified Chinese on Sohu, a popular mobile news platform in China, claims that 500 US troops stationed in Taiwan were to be withdrawn rapidly.

blocks.caption: An automated translation of a misleading article on alleged withdrawal of US troopsImage: sohu.com

blocks.text: According to a March 2026 report by the US government's Defense Manpower Data Center, 45 American military personnel are currently stationed in Taiwan.
Retired US Navy Rear Admiral Mark Montgomery stated during a hearing in May 2025 that 500 American military personnel were providing training in Taiwan.

DW Fact check reached out to Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense, which declined to comment. The US Department of Defense and the Pentagon did not respond to requests for comment by the time of publication.
Distorted quotes and misleading clips
Claim: A TikTok video claims to show US president Donald Trump saying the US is abandoning Taiwan.

blocks.caption: In this TikTok video, Donald Trump's response in an interview was interpreted beyond what the US president had actually saidImage: tiktok.com

blocks.text: The original video was from a Fox News interview​​​​​​​Fox News interview with Trump on May 16. The interviewer did not ask whether the United States would defend Taiwan, and the US president did not comment on the issue.

Trump said he did not want Taiwan to become independent or for a war to break out, adding that the status quo should be maintained to allow tensions to de-escalate. He also clearly stated that his policy toward Taiwan "has not changed." Washington has long maintained a policy of strategic ambiguity toward Taiwan– neither explicitly guaranteeing the island's defense nor ruling out the possibility of doing so.

articles.title: Bill to teach students Critical Media and Info Literacy aims to counter fake news
articles.summary: A bill requiring a Critical Media and Information Literacy subject across all levels of the Philippine educational system has been filed in the House of Representatives.

blocks.text: Published November 25, 2026 6:33pm
A bill requiring a Critical Media and Information Literacy subject across all levels of the Philippine educational system has been filed in the House of Representatives.
House Deputy Minority Leader Antonio Tinio of ACT Teachers party-list and Representatives Sarah Elago of Gabriela and Renee Co of Kabataan made the proposal under House Bill 12061.

The authors said that the Critical Media and Information Literacy subject would cover topics beyond basic technical or analytical skills and critical media literacy, and involves an ideological critique of media representations, an analysis of power dynamics underpinning information control, and the activeproduction of alternative media.

The authors said the measure is urgent given that information is now easily digested through posts, tweets, and videos seen in various social media platforms, a situation that has led to the democratization of information production and dissemination—but also one that can be controlled by powerful political and economic actors to systematically manufacture public consent and distort reality at the same time.

“There is a prevalence of Al-generated content, in which individuals can freely alter data, structure its legitimacy, imitating information produced by authorized media institutions. Without thorough assessment and fact-checking, it is no longer unacceptable to say that the public is exposed to a wide variety of news, the truthfulness of which ranging from most reliable to most questionable,” the bill read.

The lawmakers said the advent of sophisticated artificial intelligence (AI) tools has also exponentially increased the scale and believability of fabricated content, from deepfake videos to Al-generated news articles, creating an environment where distinguishing fact from malicious fiction requires advanced analytical skills.

“This bill seeks to transform Filipino students from passive recipients of information into empowered, critical citizens capable of defending democratic discourse from manipulation and fostering a culture of truth-seeking and civic engagement,” the bill added.
Co, for her part, said the subject will train students to go beyond memorization and sharpen comprehension.
"Dapat sanayin ang bawat estudyante na kumwestiyon, mag-imbestiga, at sumalungat sa kasinungalingan. Huwag tayo basta na lang mag-scroll at maniwala sa kung ano ang nakikita sa screen," Co said.
(We should train our students to ask questions, investigate and fight lies. We must learn not to simply scroll and believe everything we see online.)
"Pag mulat at kritikal ang kabataan, hindi sila basta-basta mabubudol ng mga fake news peddlers. Sila mismo ang magiging bantay ng katotohanan at demokrasya," she added.
(If the students are aware and critical, they won't easily fall to fake news peddlers. Instead, they will be the guardrails of truth and democracy.)
— BM, GMA News

articles.title: Ashes or sand? John Arcilla goes to NBI to check pets' remains in wake of dumped carcasses in Bulacan
articles.summary: Actor John Arcilla went to the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) on Wednesday to seek the bureau"s help in authenticating the ashes of two of his pets. Arcilla made the move weeks after the…

blocks.text: Published November 25, 2026 6:21pm
Actor John Arcilla went to the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) on Wednesday to seek the bureau’s help in authenticating the ashes of two of his pets.
Arcilla made the move weeks after the remains of more than 20 dogs and cats were found dumped along a road in Bulacan. Authorities discovered that the carcasses were supposed to have been cremated.

“Iniisip ko kung nangyari ‘yon sa Bulacan, sandali lang, ito bang kini-keep ko ang ilang taon na to… baka mamaya sand lang to? Anong klaseng ash lang to? So gusto kong ipa-check dito sa NBI,” Arcilla told reporters.
(I was thinking, if that happened in Bulacan, wait a minute—what I’ve been keeping all these years, could this just be sand? What kind of ash is this? So I wanted to have it checked here at the NBI.)

He clarified that he did not avail himself of the services of Ahjay Paws Aftercare Pet Crematorium in Bacoor City, Cavite, which is currently being investigated for allegedly dumping the remains found in Bulacan.

The actor shared that 12 of his pets were cremated across different crematoriums, and even though he has kept their urns for nearly a decade, he grew paranoid that the ashes of the animals, whom he considers family, might not be real either.

“Kasi magmula nung nangyari yung sa Bulacan, bigla kang nagkaroon ng paranoia na—kasi 12 na kasi yung dogs ko na pina-cremate ko pero tatlong crematorium.. Ayokong i-divulge ‘yung name yet kasi hindi pa naman ako sure, kaya lang gusto ko lang kasing ma-sure na yung ashes na nasa akin [ay sila talaga],” Arcilla said.

(Because ever since what happened in Bulacan, you suddenly get paranoid—I’ve had 12 dogs cremated across three crematoriums. I don’t want to divulge the names yet because I’m not sure, I just want to be certain that the ashes in my possession are really theirs.)
He shared that it took him a while before deciding to have the ashes of his departed pets tested, as he did not know how he would feel if the results turned out negative.
However, the actor stressed that he also felt a responsibility to find out whether the cremation services he availed were legitimate so he could warn future clients if they were not.

“Kasi mamaya yung resulta hindi ko gusto, anong mararamdaman ko? Anong gagawin ko doon sa aking isang sacred space a 12 yung family member ko na anandoon tapos kini-keep ko ng almost a decade na and wala na akong balak na itapon sya kasi hindi naman yon basura eh,” Arcilla said.

(What if the results aren’t what I want, how will I feel? What will I do with that sacred space of mine where my 12 family members are kept, which I’ve maintained for nearly a decade and have no intention of throwing away because they aren’t trash?)
“Pag napatunayan kong hindi pala totoo yon, edi i have to save the other clients of that pet crematorium,” he added.
(If I prove that they aren’t real, then I have to save the other clients of that pet crematorium.)

Last week, the NBI found that the urns provided to pet owners by the controversial Cavite pet crematorium did not contain animal remains, prompting several owners to file complaints before the Department of Justice.
Its owners and other individuals involved now face charges of estafa and violations of the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act. —NB, GMA News

articles.title: They bought this N.S. bungalow as a fixer-upper. It was just demolished without their knowledge
articles.summary: A bungalow nestled on the outskirts of Springhill, N.S., was a pandemic purchase for a couple, but they were surprised to return this fall to find all buildings and irreplaceable mementoes on the…

image.caption: The couple installed a new roof and put a fresh coat of paint on the door of the home, but after two years away the grass was overgrown. (Municipality of Cumberland)

blocks.text: Nova Scotia

A bungalow nestled on the outskirts of Springhill, N.S., was a pandemic purchase for a couple, but they were surprised to return this fall to find all buildings and irreplaceable mementoes on the property gone.
Staff in northern N.S. county left notices, but owners were away for more than 2 years

A bungalow nestled on the outskirts of Springhill, N.S., was a pandemic purchase with potential for a first-generation Canadian couple, but they were surprised to return to Nova Scotia this fall to find their buildings and irreplaceable mementoes gone.
Ksenia Sabouloua and Phil Karounos bought the 4.8-hectare property sight unseen for just over $30,000 in July 2020.
The couple has worked in Ontario and the Northwest Territories but had never been to Nova Scotia, let alone the former coal mining community in Cumberland County.
The bungalow was a fixer-upper, but Sabouloua and her partner Karounos saw potential for starting a small farm.
“The East Coast was just somewhere that I always wanted to live. It's just so beautiful,” said Sabouloua in an interview.

Karounos said the home was ready for electrical fixtures and kitchen cabinets, but they ran out of money. He said the work they did to that point included shingling the roof, rewiring the home and installing a new subfloor — estimating they spent up to $30,000 on the renovations.
They didn't have enough money to finish the project all at once, and found better-paying jobs outside of Nova Scotia to help save for more renovations.
In October, they returned to the fixer-upper for the first time in more than two years.
Demolition order
To their surprise, all that was left was a muddy lot.
They found utility lines sticking up from the ground, a compost bin and pieces of debris strewn about the property.
“It was just shocking to come home. Right. That's our home no matter what,” Sabouloua said.
In August, the Municipality of Cumberland council voted to issue a demolition order for the home and a camper located on the property. The work was completed by early September.
Sabouloua said the most heartbreaking loss is not financial, but deeply personal family items stored in a shed that was also demolished.
“Pictures from Russia where I was born. All the way to my Carleton graduation diploma. So, like, just when I'm saying everything … I don't have anything,” she said, choking back tears.

In his presentation at council, director of protective services Allen Cole said the couple did not respond to notices posted on the door of the bungalow and letters mailed to another address about the potential demolition.
PHOTOS | A vacant lot is all that remains of this fixer-upper:
The staff report showed images of a hole in the side of the home and no subfloor.
Karounos said a new patio door installed in the house was also removed.
The report also said the camper was trashed on the inside.
The couple said that is not how they left it in June 2024.

“I just can't understand how this was fair. We were the victims of crime. There was obvious vandalism and all these other things, and also that there seems to be no response from the RCMP,” said Korounos.
Multiple neighbours told CBC News people were squatting at the property while the couple was away.
They also said the home was severely vandalized earlier this year — something the couple said they were not aware of until informed by the CBC.
Complaint to police
Nova Scotia RCMP said officers attended the property once in the past two years.

In June 2026, a complaint was received about the camper’s proximity to the road. Officers reported there were indications someone was living there and photographs were sent to the county through email.

“Officers confirmed through property records that the owner's listed address was in Ontario. The information forwarded to the municipality related to concerns about the condition of the property and potential safety issues observed by officers,” said an RCMP spokesperson in a statement.
The couple admit that their address was out of date but question why officials did not make more of an effort to get in touch with them.

Ksenia Sabouloua and partner Phil Karounos spent more than $50,000 to buy and fix up a small home in Springhill, N.S. After a stint away working, the couple returned to continue the project only to find it demolished. (Toni Choueiri/CBC)
Korounos said his current email address is the same one he used to communicate with the county permitting department in 2021.
The home was also slated for tax sale in October — something the couple said was an oversight on their part.
In that case Sabouloua said the county communicated with her bank who in turn contacted her. But by the time the back taxes were paid on Sept. 24, the home had already been gone for weeks.
Complaint driven

Allen Cole, who oversees dangerous or unsightly premises at the county, told CBC News he could not speak to the couple's specific order because it could become subject to litigation, such as a judicial review.

In an interview, Cole said staff do title searches and in some cases attempt to find property owners on social media. He said county records show just shy of 10 per cent of demolition orders issued have unresponsive property owners.

items: More stories from Northern Nova Scotia

blocks.text: “Unless there is an issue of immediate danger, we only deal with properties for which we have received a complaint from the public,” said Cole.

“The cases are not brought to council lightly. There's significant due diligence put into every single one of these cases,” he said, noting there's been an average of about one demolition order per month since 2024.
Cole said the cost of the demolition is added to the property owner's next annual tax bill.

Sabouloua said they have no idea what that bill will be, and are still sorting out what to do next. She said it is shocking to learn how quickly the county's demolition order came after the police received a complaint, and yet they heard nothing until it was too late.
"We would have started to resolve this right away. Even if everything was stolen and the door was gone," she said.
"I would have loved to have finished it up."

articles.title: Climate loss and damage fund exists, but the money doesn't
articles.summary: Climate-vulnerable countries fought for years to create a loss and damage fund. Four years on, demand far outstrips funding, pledges are scarce, and disaster-hit nations are still waiting for support.

image.caption: Nepal in the aftermath of August flash floods that killed more than 1,500 people, with thousands more missingImage: Arun Sankar/AFP

blocks.text: On the sandbars and river islands of Bangladesh's Brahmaputra and its branches, families have little to fall back on when the water rises.
"The floodwater swallows everything," said 16-year-old Rasel Babu who had traveled to Antalya, Turkey to speak to delegates at the UN climate conference.

Created after years of pressure from vulnerable nations, the loss and damage fund was designed to help countries recover from climate disasters and irreversible climate impacts. This includes extreme weather events such as floods, heat waves and wildfires as well as slow onset impacts such as sea level rise, desertification and damage to infrastructure and crops.
But the fund is already struggling to meet demand. It received $2.8 billion (€2.56 billion) in urgent requests in a first call for funding, with only $342 million available at the time.
Even the money promised has not fully arrived. Only about half of the money currently pledged had been received by this summer.

While the European Commission signed a €25 million ($27 million) contribution agreement to the fund on the margins of COP31, formalizing an earlier pledge made at COP28, and Spain pledged an additional €15 million, other contributions to loss and damage remained scarce.
First payout will go to Nepal after glacier collapse

The fund's first emergency response is going to be paid out to Nepal. The board of the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage had provisionally set aside $21.6 million following the catastrophic glacier collapse that triggered flash floods in August, killing more than 1,500 people with 5,600 more missing.
But the money has not moved yet. Nepal must first submit a funding request setting out how it will be spent.

"It's asking for a country that is dealing with the climate emergency to work on a proposal," Nepali climate finance expert Bibek Raj Kandel said, adding a layer of bureaucracy inefficient to address the urgency.
UN warns climate change could force millions to move

Nepal is already waiting on another request, filed after floods in Kathmandu and landslides in the eastern hills. "There's already one pending proposal sitting on the table," Kandel said. Unless the fund speeds up, he warned, it's "going to disappoint many, many countries."
Pakistan which led the push for the fund in 2022 after floods affected 33 million people and killed more than 1,730, also hasn't seen any of the money yet.

"Pakistan was one of the countries which really spoke up and managed to get the loss and damage fund on the climate agenda. But it takes a long time," Pakistan's Minister of State for Climate Change, Shezra Mansab Ali Khan Kharal, told DW.

blocks.caption: In 2022, monsoon and floods killed more than 1,730 people in Pakistan, with 33 million people affectedImage: Akhtar Soomro/REUTERS

blocks.text: "We have still not really got anything. We haven't seen anything on the ground at all as yet," Kharal said. Pakistan has submitted two projects and was told the cap is $200 million.
Other forms of aid often come in the form of loans.

"These promises, they are hollow promises," said Abid Qaiyum Suleri, Executive Director of the Sustainable Development Policy Institute (SDPI) in Islamabad, adding that for a heavily indebted country, the form of the money matters as much as the amount.
"We do not want that a climate disaster in Pakistan should translate into further debt for Pakistan," Kharal said, calling for grants rather than loans.

articles.title: More connected but lonelier than ever: How do we navigate an AI-reliant world?
articles.summary: Mental health advocates say that tools like AI chatbots normalize isolation and provide a false sense of connection. Where do we draw the line, especially for the youth?

blocks.text: Mental health advocates say that tools like AI chatbots normalize isolation and provide a false sense of connection. Where do we draw the line, especially for the youth?

items: The rise of artificial intelligence and social media has transformed childhood experiences, leading to increased reliance on screens and AI chatbots for companionship and support.
Mental health advocates express concern that AI chatbots may normalize isolation and prevent meaningful human connections, particularly among children and vulnerable individuals.
Experts emphasize the need for a systemic approach to address the impact of technology on mental health, advocating for stronger community support and human-centered policies.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
Childhood looks different for many kids nowadays in the age of artificial intelligence and social media.

Toys are no longer the only things keeping them busy. Screens dominate their free time. And when they want to play with their friends, they don’t always just head outside anymore; they log onto gaming platforms instead.

And when they become lonely and need someone to open up to, it’s no longer a human hearing them out — but an AI chatbot. For mental health advocates like actress and She Talks Asia co-founder Iza Calzado, the rise of these tools is alarming. Under the guise of connection and offering safe spaces, AI chatbots often just work to normalize isolation, and it’s a reality that many humans who have fallen for the trap have to face.

“It’s safer to chat with a bot in this landscape. It agrees with you all the time. It does not judge you. It’s never disappointed when you say something. So imagine a child, who perhaps does not feel as confident or as safe in their own home, is lonely, starts talking to a bot, and then eventually becomes friends with a bot,” Calzado illustrated during a panel discussion at Rappler’s 2026 Social Good Summit last Saturday, November 21.
“Because you know what? This friend will not unfriend me, will not spread rumors about me in school, and will not bully me. That’s how it begins, and that to me is very concerning.”

Even among adults, AI chatbots have become pseudo-therapists who help rationalize their thoughts, make sense of whatever they’re going through, and validate their feelings — even when they may be in the wrong. The chatbot pulls you in by making you feel seen, and before you know it, you’ve been completely hooked.
But why does it do this?
For Empath CEO and founder Steph Naval, it’s simple: AI chatbots are there to make money.

blocks.caption: Steph Naval at We the Humans, Social Good Summit at BGC, Taguig City, on November 20, 2026.

blocks.text: “Chatbots, when you go there for a replacement of therapy or well-being, what happens is that you don’t get the benefit of having difficult conversations and corrective behavior. Because that’s something that you do in therapy,” Naval said, adding that it was in her painful therapy sessions that she was actually able to heal and grow most.

blocks.caption: Unpacking mental health chats with AI: Finding comfort, but not treatment

blocks.text: It’s the same with social media, which has become a fierce breeding ground for insecurity. Naval said these apps can detect that through your images and videos, and “responds by pushing certain products or content that can exacerbate these negative thoughts.

“For example, it takes a lot of photos of your body or the gym and then they can detect if you feel insecure. Then they’ll push products to you. So I find that’s something to definitely take note of because that has really caused and affected a generation,” said Naval.

Social media and chatbots, however, don’t just offer you a false sense of companionship and feed on your biggest vulnerabilities. They have also doubled a platform for groups to promote violence among young children — and this is something that has become apparent in the alarming rise of school shooting incidents in the Philippines.

blocks.caption: [Be The Good] Not another school shooting please

blocks.text: Still, Akbayan Representative Perci Cendaña believes that the growing reliance on these chatbots isn’t something you can blame on those who turn to it, especially in countries like the Philippines where mental health services are scarce. From then on, it only leads to a bigger set of issues that the country is not yet equipped to properly address.

“We lack mental health assistance, that’s why our countrymen go online instead. They rely on chatbots. They rely on the warmth and affirmation they get from these platforms, and this phenomenon, combined with other social realities, are fueling these isolated incidents,” Cendaña said in a mix of Filipino and English.
“Nauuna ang teknolohiya sa polisiya. Nauuna ang teknolohiya sa government framework (Technology is prioritized over policy. Technology is ahead of the government framework),” he added.

blocks.caption: Perci Cendaña at We the Humans, Social Good Summit at BGC, Taguig City, on November 20, 2026.

blocks.text: This is what Cendaña hopes to address through the National AI Governance Act — which is anchored on human-centeredness. It contains the AI Bill of Rights, which holds that humans should have the authority to override platform systems.

Cendaña then believes that tech executives and government officials shouldn’t be the only ones making decisions about AI governance. Because it’s human well-being at the very core of it all, civil society should have a seat at the table, too.

The solutions to the impact of AI and technology on community mental health requires an intensive systemic approach. But these policies are not what we should only rely on, because these safeguards should start at home.
“Home should be the safest space. That’s the first line of defense — families, friends… So let’s make sure that we are that for our children,” Calzado said.

blocks.caption: Iza Calzado at We the Humans, Social Good Summit at BGC, Taguig City, on November 20, 2026.

blocks.text: Parents need their own community, too, however. It takes more than a village to raise a child in this era, and parents also need their own kind of support and human connection so they can come home strong to their kids.

For Naval, one of the best ways to do that is to dedicate time to activities that will allow you to interact with other human beings. Take a wellness class. Join clubs for your hobbies. Make the effort to see your friends in person.
Technology and AI are here to stay. Decentering it, then, requires us to go back to our roots as humans and hone in on that. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Germany's women's football team take stand against domestic violence
articles.summary: Germany's women's football team are to wear UN Women badges in games against Argentina and Peru, as domestic violence hits a record high in Germany.

image.caption: Germany's women have been strong supporters of the campaign, as the orange logo of 'stop violence agianst women' reveals on Lea Schüller's sleeveImage: imago images/Beautiful Sports

blocks.text: Domestic violence has reached a record high in Germany, with 16 women subjected to physical abuse behind closed doors each hour.

UN Women Germany is one of 13 UN Women national committees worldwide, each an independent, non-profit, non-governmental organization committed to gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls.

Their current campaign "Orange The World" runs from the start of International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women on November 25 to December 10, International Human Rights Day. It is designed to raise awareness around violence against women in the country and worldwide. The 2026 campaign's focus is particularly on men's responsibility in ending gender-based violence.

"In these 16 days of activism, we can deliver a lot of information. Survivors of gender-based violence can find out where to get support and be reminded that they are not at fault," UN Women Germany chair, politician and long-standing campaigner for women's rights Elke Ferner told DW. "The debate helps and it's a chance to change consciousness about the topic."

Germany captain Giulia Gwinn said in a statement via the German Football Association (DFB): "Violence against women and girls affects us all and must have no place in our society. As the women's national team, we therefore want to once again use our reach to create awareness for this important issue and jointly set a visible sign against violence."
The campaign with the women's team is not new. Two years ago, the team joined the campaign, delivering a moving video that saw players reveal the truth of statements by crossing out words.

During Germany's upcoming South America tour — part of their preparations for the 2027 World Cup in Brazil — they are to wear special UN Women Germany badges on their sleeves in their games against Argentina and Peru.
Role models pivotal for the campaign

Ferner believes the work with role models is pivotal and that the campaign is powerful, especially in a football context. A 2022 study from Warwick Business School in the UK revealed alcohol-related domestic abuse rises by nearly 50% after England's men's football team win a World Cup game, never mind lose.

Currently, there is no data on domestic abuse during Germany games, however during the 2026 World Cup last summer, Berlin police recorded a 31% increase in domestic violence compared to the week before.

Ferner is encouraged that sport has understood the importance of the issue, and that the German Olympic Committee (DOSB) and other sports clubs and organizations are helping move the conversation forward.

In sport, this is particularly important given the problematic nature of dependency relationships that so often exist in high-performance environments. But violence against women is really a societal issue that is not specific to class, origin, religion or societal space, such as sport.

"Violence against women has structural origins and to change that you need to change the structures," Ferner said. "You just need to do it. I always say, this isn't about a lack of knowledge but rather a lack of action."
Performance is an integral part of sport, but a multi-dimensional understanding of it might help shift perspective in a country that remains driven by a performance culture.

"What is performance? Higher, faster, further? Or is it managing to look after a family of three?" Ferner asked. "Why do people who repair washing machines earn more than those looking after your kids in nursery? This is about changing business culture, but also awareness around the role men play at home and in the family.

"The picture boys and young men get of girls and women in school is a problem that needs addressing. We can't wait for generational change. This is about saving lives. We need to change societal structures."
Male power structures a problem

Sports structures are also in need of reform. Non-profit organization Safe Sport provides independent support for people affected by sexual, physical and psychological violence in both amateur and professional sport in Germany.

They are the only organization with a specific focus on violence in grassroots sports in Germany, and one of only two in professional sport in the country. They also have to contend with structures, in a sporting context, that make spaces less safe for women.

"Gender roles have become more fluid in the last few years, but in associations and clubs management positions are still occupied by men, regardless of the sport," Safe Sport manager Ina Lambert told DW.
"In professional sport, there are a lot fewer women involved in training and so the space remains male dominated, and, as a result, so do the power structures.

"We have people in search of advice, men included, who see the problems and want to enforce change, and we offer them support so they are not alone," Lambert said. "But whether in a big association or a small club, perpetrators are frequently protected, incidents are ignored and so the people who want to enforce change are often prevented from doing so."

Safe Sport, which provides free psychological and legal support, has only been in action since July 2023, but in that time the number of support requests they have received continues to grow. Psychological violence in sport in Germany is the most common case they are faced with, but sexual violence is also a major problem.
"There is finally recognition of the problem and there is a seriousness about tackling it," Lambert said.

"There is a lot of good work being done in the right direction, with many good concepts for prevention, intervention and processing violence, as well as more education, holistic training and focus on women's menstrual cycles."

blocks.caption: Germany is backing UN efforts to highlight that more must be done to tackle violence against womenImage: imago images/Lucca Fundel

blocks.text: Comprehensive support on the way

Germany's Interior Ministry is leading the process with participants from the country's states, organized sport, affected parties and academia to create a central hub. The center for safe sport was founded in July 2026, but investigative and sanctioning work is expected to begin in the spring of 2027.
Support from leading figures clearly makes a huge difference, but it's also clear that more data is needed. Addressing the underlying issues, such as social norms and gender stereotyping, is a must.

After all, as UN Women Executive Director Sima Bahous said: "No country has yet eliminated violence against women. Ending it requires transformative action — greater investment, innovation, and unwavering political will."
This article was originally published on November 28, 2024, and updated on November 25, 2026.

articles.title: All hostages rescued after Colombian security forces storm supermarket, says president
articles.summary:
Operation in which one hostage-taker was killed ends daylong siege in Cartegena shopping centre, where 30 people were initially held

Colombian security forces have stormed a supermarket in…

blocks.text: Colombian security forces have stormed a supermarket in the Caribbean city of Cartagena, ending a daylong hostage siege, with the president saying all those held had been rescued and one hostage-taker killed.
Several explosions were heard before security forces entered the building, where about 20 people were believed to be being held by armed men.
President Abelardo de la Espriella, said: “In an extraordinary joint operation between the national police and the armed forces, all the hostages were rescued.”

Shortly after midnight on Wednesday, a police helicopter was hovering low over the shopping centre as security forces massed outside the supermarket. Explosions then echoed around the complex as tactical teams moved in.
Ten of an estimated 30 people that were initially held had already been released during the 17-hour standoff, including several elderly women.
Moments later, soldiers could be seen inside the Éxito supermarket as security forces secured the building.

De la Espriella, who appeared at the scene wearing fatigues and carrying a sidearm and a walkie-talkie, described the operation as a success. He said: “We gave them the opportunity to surrender and free the hostages. They rejected that opportunity and we acted decisively.”
Cartagena’s mayor said all the hostages were “safe and sound” and would be reunited with their families before undergoing medical checks.
The siege gripped Cartagena, a Caribbean port famed for its colonial walled old town, beach resorts and cruise-ship tourism. Supermarket employees had been among those feared trapped inside.

blocks.caption: Hostages inside the supermarket. Photograph: Sergio Jimenez Ciro/EPA

blocks.text: “My son is there,” Jacob Pérez, the father of one of the workers, said earlier in the standoff. “He didn’t leave work and he’s not answering his phone. I think they took it from him.”
Images broadcast by Colombian media and shared online appeared to show masked gunmen in tactical gear alongside zip-tied hostages inside the store.

De la Espriella was quick to rule out the involvement of guerrilla or paramilitary groups. “It’s not that a terrorist group carried out a kidnapping – no, these are criminals who were caught off guard, had no way out, and then kidnapped a group of people,” he said.
Authorities said the siege began after an attempted robbery on an armoured vehicle at the shopping centre.

According to local media, the hostage-takers were demanding nearly US$2m (£1.5m), two armoured vehicles and safe passage to the city of Barranquilla, about 80 miles (130km) north-east of Cartagena. AFP could not independently verify those reports.

The siege began on the 10th anniversary of Colombia’s landmark peace accord with Farc guerrillas amid a series of attacks across the country. Despite the deal to end the region’s largest insurgency, dissident guerrilla groups and criminal organisations still fight for control of parts of the country.
On Monday, authorities blamed a dissident Farc faction for a car bomb attack in the city of Villavicencio that wounded 25 people and caused extensive damage.

Separately, the presidency said a “terrorist attack” on electrical infrastructure had disrupted power supplies in several south-western departments and prompted additional measures to protect energy facilities.

articles.title: Burnham’s devolution plans risk ‘significant disparities’ for people in England, MPs say – UK politics live
articles.summary:
Public accounts committee warns of ‘disparities in opportunities and outcomes’ depending on the type of strategic authority where people live

Good morning. Kemi Badenoch will be choosing…

blocks.text: Good morning. Kemi Badenoch will be choosing what to raise at PMQs this morning and she’s spoilt for choice.
It would be very surprising if she did not raise the most important story of the morning – the news that gas and electricity prices will rise by 26% from January under Ofgem’s latest price cap.

But Badenoch is also interested in welfare spending, and yesterday’s publication of the Timms report has left MPs still puzzling about what the government will propose for benefits reform when it publishes its white paper next year.
Burnham himself has two announcements of his own today.

items: He has launched a Hillsborough-style investigation to examine a programme of blood tests on service personnel during nuclear weapons trials, which he said had been the subject of a “criminal cover-up on an industrial scale”.
And he has called recent high-profile rape trials a “watershed moment” for the UK and has opened the door to a wider ban on non-disclosure agreements.

blocks.text: And, as someone who is herself over-focused on social media, it is likely that Badenoch will also want to raise the row about TikTok influencers in Downing Street. It is a story about preposterous media figures with no respect for the political establishment; but that’s enough about tabloid editors for now.

One thing unlikely to come up is the public accounts committee report out today on devolving power in England. So let’s give it some coverage anyway. Burnham has many political ambitions, but the one idea that seems to matter to him more than any other, and that marks him out from his predecessors, is his desire to devolve power out of Westminster, to let mayors and other local leaders have more clout and – via this devolution – to promote growth “in every postcode”.
But, given the way the policy is being implemented, this may not happen, says the committee, which has a Labour majority. It says:

double quotation markThere is a risk of significant disparities in opportunities and outcomes for people living in different parts of England, depending on what type of strategic authority they have. The government has consciously adopted a differentiated approach to devolution. Areas that choose an elected mayor to lead their strategic authority (‘mayoral strategic authorities’) can access a broader range of devolved powers and funding flexibilities to improve local outcomes than those without a mayor. However, even among areas with a mayor, powers and arrangements differ. Only seven of England’s 18 mayoral strategic authorities receive an integrated settlement – a single funding pot for each area, collectively worth around £15.9bn up to 2029–30, that provides greater funding flexibilities and multi-year funding certainty. London also differs from other mayoral areas. Its constituent boroughs have no formal role in the Greater London Authority’s decisions or vote on its budget. This risks decisions being taken without formal input from the boroughs that are responsible for delivering local services, and may make lines of accountability less clear for local people. Fiscal devolution could further deepen differences between areas. The government’s October 2026 Fiscal Devolution Roadmap confirms that only mayoral strategic authorities will be able to retain a share of local income tax. It proposes ways to limit disparities between different mayoral strategic authorities, but important details are still to be determined, including through the next spending review, and it therefore remains uncertain how effective these arrangements will be.
Here is the agenda for the day.
Noon: Andy Burnham faces Kemi Badenoch at PMQs.
3pm: Nigel Farage and Arron Banks launch their Keep Britain Out campaign opposing the idea of the UK rejoining the EU.

I’m afraid we are no longer able to have comments open below the line every day on this blog. If you want to contact me, please email politics.live@theguardian.com. You can use this email to flag up corrections, comments for publication, questions or complaints.

articles.title: ‘Russia wants more than Ukraine,’ Germany’s Merz warns – Europe live
articles.summary:
German chancellor, in wide-ranging speech, says Moscow is ‘escalating on a massive scale’

Merz also touches on this week’s EU summit, starting tomorrow, and the likely…

blocks.text: 'Russia wants more than Ukraine,' Germany's Merz warns, as he says Moscow is 'escalating on a massive scale'

In his wide-ranging budget speech, Merz talks about Germany “neglecting fundamental issues for far too long” on defence, infrastructure, demographic change, and the economy – and the need to address these issues urgently.
But the starkest part of his speech comes as he talks about the external situation – and particularly the threat from Russia - to explain why some decisions, particularly on defence, are needed.
“Russia knows exactly what it wants and Russia wants more than Ukraine,” he warns.

“Anyone who fails to grasp this either does not understand the world as it is, or is pursuing an entirely different agenda – one that stands in opposition to the freedom, openness, and liberal values ​​of our own country.”
Merz warns that “Russia is escalating tensions in the Baltic region, in Poland, in the Black Sea, and even in the outer space.”

“It is escalating on a massive scale – including here within our own borders, even at the cost of human lives. That is the situation, ladies and gentlemen. And that is why we, as Europeans, must—and will – set clear boundaries for Russia.”
Key events

items: 14m agoGermany has 'begun to change course' amid major challenges, Merz says
22m ago'By supporting Ukraine, we are supporting and protecting ourselves,' Merz tells parliament
26m ago'Russia wants more than Ukraine,' Germany's Merz warns, as he says Moscow is 'escalating on a massive scale'
37m agoMorning opening: Ukraine reporting energy outages in five regions after Russian strikes

blocks.text: Germany has 'begun to change course' amid major challenges, Merz says
Merz also touches on this week’s EU summit, starting tomorrow, and the likely contentious negotiations over the next EU budget.
He pushes back on “impressions” that he thinks Germany spends too much on EU contributions.
But he says he is “pushing for us to limit and focus our spending on what truly strengthens Europe today,” specifically on security and competitiveness.

In a pretty passionate defence of European integration, he says only such focused spending will give Europe “an assurance that we will not simply become a plaything in this world, but have a hand in shaping it.”

Summing up, he repeats his earlier point that Germany faces major challenges that have been unresolved for too long, and so one budget “is far from solving all of our problems,” but says “we have begun to change course” as economic indicators are starting to improve.
And he ends his speech there.

blocks.caption: German chancellor Friedrich Merz takes a drink of water as he sits down after his speech. Photograph: Odd Andersen/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: 'By supporting Ukraine, we are supporting and protecting ourselves,' Merz tells parliament

Merz goes back to last week’s meeting of the Coalition of the Willing in Berlin, saying the US delegation was “it seemed to me, quite clearly surprised by how united … the Europeans are on this issue.”
“It is precisely this determination, ladies and gentlemen, that allows for a cautious optimism regarding the prospect of peace – a genuine peace,” he says.
He keeps coming back to his main message: “by supporting Ukraine, we are supporting and protecting ourselves.”
“This is true in a sense that may not yet be fully understood by many in our country,” he stresses.
Germany’s chancellor Friedrich Merz is speaking in the Bundestag now – mostly on the 2027 budget, but he’s also touching upon broader issues, including on Russia and Ukraine.

blocks.caption: German chancellor Friedrich Merz speaks on the day of the 2027 budget debate at the German lower house of parliament, the Bundestag, in Berlin. Photograph: Liesa Johannssen/Reuters

blocks.text: I will bring you key quotes here.
Morning opening: Ukraine reporting energy outages in five regions after Russian strikes

blocks.caption: Jakub Krupa

blocks.text: Jakub Krupa
Russian strikes ⁠on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure overnight caused ⁠power ⁠outages in ​five regions, deputy energy minister ⁠Artem Nekrasov said this morning.

blocks.caption: Local residents stand outside a damaged residential building following a Russian air strike that killed two and wounded another 40 in the centre of Zaporizhzhia yesterday. Photograph: AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: The ⁠affected regions are ​Dnipropetrovsk, ‌Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, Odesa ‌and Kharkiv. The ‌situation is most difficult in the Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk regions, he said, as reported by Reuters.
Separately, at least two people were killed in a strike in Odesa, and injuries were reported in Kyiv after a strike on a multi-storey apartment in the capital.
The latest attacks come just hours before Nato’s secretary general Mark Rutte is due to meet with the US president, Donald Trump, in Mar-A-Lago for talks behind the closed doors.
Their meeting comes amid reported delays in air defence missile deliveries to Ukraine, as the country braces for a tough winter under continuing Russian assaults.
I will bring you all the latest here.
It’s Wednesday, 25 November 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.
Good morning.

articles.title: DOJ seeks to retain P100 daily food allowance for inmates in 2027
articles.summary: The allowance was last adjusted under the 2026 budget.

blocks.text: November 25, 2026 | 5:09pm
Newly transferred inmates at the Iwahig Prison and Penal Farm on March 27, 2026.
Bureau of Corrections / Released
MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Justice has proposed retaining the P100-per-day food allowance for persons deprived of liberty (PDLs) in its 2027 budget.

Sen. Francisco "Kiko" Pangilinan, sponsor of the department’s budget, confirmed the proposal during the Senate budget hearing on Wednesday, November 25, saying the amount would remain the same "despite the rising prices."
Asked by Sen. Vicente “Tito” Sotto if the allowance would suffice, Pangilinan explained that the DOJ had issued a department order to implement the Sagip Saka Act in its concerned offices.
The law allows government offices to purchase produce and other agricultural goods directly from farmers and fisherfolk without the need for public bidding.
Full implementation would allow them to reduce food costs, as market prices of produce, according to Pangilinan, are around triple the goods’ farmgate rates.
The department, meanwhile, moved to increase the medical allowance to P30 from P20.
This allowance does not cover the gynecological needs of female PDLs.
Instead, these needs are charged to the PDLs’ hygiene allowance, which has been P3,000 per year since 2022.
The Commission on Human Rights has previously called on legislators to adapt PDL allowances to current economic challenges.

In October 2026, inflation soared to 7.8%, the highest rate seen in almost four years. For rice and corn—which comprise more than 92% of agricultural damage attributed to the Super El Niño so far—inflation accelerated to 20.7% from 20.3% and 19.3% from 17.3%, respectively.
The impact of these losses will be reflected in the Philippine Statistics Authority's inflation data for November 2026.
