articles.title: Senate prioritizes feeding program in push for higher 2027 DepEd budget
articles.summary: Senator Bam Aquino wants to increase the school-based feeding program's budget to P28.7 billion. Meanwhile, the ARAL Program has no allocation in the Senate committee report.

blocks.text: BUDGET DEBATES. Senator Bam Aquino and Education Secretary Sonny Angara during the Senate plenary deliberations on the proposed 2027 budget of the Department of Education on November 24, 2026.
Senate Social Media Unit
Senator Bam Aquino wants to increase the school-based feeding program's budget to P28.7 billion. Meanwhile, the ARAL Program has no allocation in the Senate committee report.

items: Senator Bam Aquino advocates for prioritizing the school-based feeding program in the 2027 budget, proposing an increase to P28.7 billion to expand coverage.
The Senate finance committee recommended a P915.49-billion budget for the Department of Education, but the ARAL Program remains unfunded.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Senator Bam Aquino recommended making the school-based feeding program the top priority for an additional budget among other Department of Education (DepEd) programs in 2027.
Overall, the Senate finance committee recommended P915.49 billion for the proposed new general appropriations of the DepEd and its attached agencies.
That amount is P4.91 billion higher than the P910.5 billion approved by the House of Representatives, but P1.25 billion lower than the P916.75 billion in the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP).
Among the changes, the Senate panel added P11 billion to the school-based feeding program, pushing the proposed allocation to P22.4 billion.

But Aquino, as the DepEd’s budget sponsor, plans to seek an additional increase for the program. “At the proper time, this representation, alongside some other colleagues, will introduce an amendment to increase the budget for the school-based feeding program by P6,265,478,145,” he said during the plenary deliberations.
That would raise the program’s budget to P28.7 billion, higher than the P25.7 billion in the 2026 national budget.

The additional funding would also expand the universal feeding to cover kindergarten to Grade 2, reaching another 1.8 million students in 2027. This follows the phased implementation under the national children’s nutrition bill, which has been ratified but not yet signed into law.
The P28.7-billion budget would cover 124 feeding days, or from June to December in 2027, at P30 per meal.

blocks.caption: After Congress, expanded nutrition program bill’s next test is funding

blocks.text: Aquino remains hopeful that they can still set a higher budget for the education sector.
“I have spoken to the Senate President multiple times to share my frustration with the fiscal space provided for this important agency,” he said in the plenary.

“We have proposed a much bigger budget only to be met with an answer that we didn’t like, which was that the fiscal space is very limited — which we understand. Mr. [Senate] President, I believe that we can still increase this before the period of amendments,” he added in a mix of English and Filipino.
Aquino also supports funding for the Academic Recovery and Accessible Learning (ARAL) Program in 2027. There is no separate line item for it in the 2027 NEP.
However, in the Senate committee report, the ARAL Program remains unfunded.
“Talo pa tayo ng House. P300 million, nakalagay sila. Tayo, wala,” Senator Joel Villanueva said during his interpellation. (The House outdid us. They allocated P300 million. We did not put anything.)
Villanueva noted that 11 million students have been identified as needing remediation sessions in school year 2026-2027.
Aquino told senators that the ARAL Program still has unspent funds from this year. During the 2026 budget talks, it was the Senate that pushed P8.9 billion for the learning recovery initiative.

“More than half of the P8.9-billion budget for this year was released very late, only in July and August. Therefore, because of the late release, meron pa pong pondo, ‘yon ang gagamitin (there is still funding, which will be used) next year,” he explained.
He added that the disbursement rate, which refers to actual payments made, is only at 13%.

According to Aquino, the DepEd is already in the process of disbursing the funds in the next few weeks, with Education Secretary Sonny Angara promising a faster process. Angara was standing beside the senator during the deliberations.
“We know that it can work. We’ve been talking about our learning gaps for so many months. The main solution to the learning gap is really a remediation program,” Aquino said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Mothers urge DOH to replenish depleted pneumococcal conjugate vaccine stocks
articles.summary: Mothers are urging the DOH to replenish depleted stocks of free pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCV), warning that supply delays are forcing parents to consider costly shots at private hospitals to…

blocks.text: November 25, 2026 | 4:02pm
MANILA, Philippines — Weeks before Christmas, several parents look forward to receiving their 13th-month pay, hoping to use it for a sumptuous Noche Buena feast.
But for some families, putting meals on the table for Christmas Eve may not be their biggest priority this year.

One of them is Emilyn Garcia (not her real name), 28, a mother of two from Negros Occidental, who would rather pay out of pocket to secure a dose of pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV) for her baby at a private hospital. This comes after vaccine supplies—which should be provided free of charge at public health centers across the country—have run dry for months.

“Maghintay lang daw po (They just told us to wait)," she said, recalling how she and her baby repeatedly visited their health center, only to be told that they had to wait for weeks for the box of vaccine vials to arrive.
“Kaya wala talagang kaming idea if ano bang problema, kung bakit wala pa rin ‘yong vaccine" Garcia told Philstar.com.
(So we really have no idea what the problem is or why the vaccine is still unavailable.)
The vaccine is part of the government’s immunization schedule for infants, with doses administered at six, 10 and 14 weeks of age.
However, Garcia’s baby has yet to receive even the first dose of PCV, despite already reaching seven months of age.

What is PCV? For parents like Garcia, the wait means more than having to forgo something extra for the holidays. The vaccine is meant to provide their children with immune protection against respiratory complications and invasive bacterial infections caused by bacteria that can colonize the nose and throat.

According to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), PCV protects against diseases such as pneumonia, as well as other serious infections, including ear infections and meningitis, to which infants are vulnerable.
Pneumonia and meningitis are among the leading causes of illness and death worldwide for children under two years old, UNICEF Philippines said.

The World Health Organization (WHO) reported that pneumonia claimed 740,180 lives in 2019, with the disease most prevalent in southern Asia and sub-Saharan Africa. Meningitis is a life-threatening disease that causes inflammation of the membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord.
The WHO added that preventive measures, including vaccination, timely diagnosis and appropriate medical care, can help protect children from the disease.
A costly alternative for parents
Despite its importance, accessing the PCV shot becomes an ordeal for mothers nationwide due to depleting stocks.

“Hinihintay ko na mag-explain kung bakit wala o magsabi sila na mayroon ba o wala [supply],” Garcia said. (I'm waiting for them to explain why it's unavailable or to tell us whether there is supply or none)
“Babies are the most vulnerable eh. Need nila ‘yan, (Babies are the most vulnerable. They need it)" she added.
If the vaccine does not arrive by the second week of December, Garcia said she would get it from private hospitals, where she was quoted between P5,000 and P6,000 per dose.
Completing the three-dose series could cost her approximately P15,000 to P18,000, an amount she said would be difficult for low-income Filipino households to afford.
Garcia called on the Department of Health (DOH) to replenish its PCV stocks, joining other mothers who demanded a clear timeline for restocking.

“[Baka dumating] sa puntong ma-hospital ang mga bata, ang mga anak namin, dahil sa isang sakit na sana ay naiwasan kung hindi lang nagkaroon ng kakulangan ang ating gobyerno,” Gigi Vargas-Baroga, 31, a first-time mother from Camarines Sur, said.
(It might reach the point where children, our own children, end up hospitalized because of an illness that could have been prevented if our government had not experienced a shortage)
“[Sana] magkaroon ng siguradong panahon, buwan, kung kailan, or sagot, definite answer kung kailan magkakaroon ng PCV,” she added.
(We hope they can give us a definite timeline or month, or a clear answer on when the PCV will become available.)
DOH says PCV vaccine deliveries are underway
Health Secretary Edwin Mercado told Philstar.com that 5.5 million doses of PCV were procured in 2026, a 400,000-dose decrease from 5.9 million in 2025.
“The vaccines are on the way. They will be in phases lang as we verify quality and safety on the vaccines,” Mercado said.
The DOH said deliveries were made on November 10 and 11 in several areas across the country, based on its supply chain management system.

Among the areas that received direct deliveries are Mimaropa and the Bicol Region, including the Legazpi City Health Office, Masbate Provincial Health Office and City Health Office, Pascual Rural Health Unit, Sorsogon Provincial Health Office and Claveria Rural Health Unit.

Other city and provincial health offices included Marawi, Tawi-Tawi, Lamitan, Maguindanao del Sur and Maguindanao del Norte, Lanao del Norte and Lanao del Sur, as well as Basilan through the Ministry of Health of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao.
Regional government health units of Western Visayas, Central Visayas, Central Luzon, Caraga, Northern Mindanao, Davao and Soccsksargen also received deliveries.

What caused the delivery delay? Jan Llevado of the DOH Disease Prevention and Control Bureau attributed the procurement delays to adjustments following the implementation of the new procurement law and concerns raised by suppliers.

“These adjustments, together with the necessary coordination and procedural processes, affected the overall procurement timeline. Concerns raised by suppliers also required careful consideration to ensure fairness, transparency, and compliance with the applicable rules,” she said in an interview Philstar.com.
Vaccine shortage amid questions over health spending

In a radio interview on November 14, Ombudsman Jesus Remulla called for transparency in the healthcare sector following reports of bulk medicine purchases that expired, even as recurring shortages in medical facilities remained a concern.
Earlier, on September 4, Sen. Raffy Tulfo revealed during a Senate hearing the alleged multibillion-peso worth of medicines purchased in 2023 that were reportedly “buried underground.”

During the House appropriations briefing on September 7, Mercado said the DOH was looking to fast-track vaccine procurement to prevent supply delays, with P6.855 billion earmarked for its immunization program.
The House of Representatives later realigned the DOH's budget during the continuation of the 2027 proposed budget deliberations on November 14.

Deputy Speaker Janette Garin (Iloilo, 1st District) cited the underutilization of vaccine funds to explain the P4.87-billion reduction in allocations for family health, immunization and nutrition commodities.
According to Garin, the funds allocated for pneumococcal vaccines for children in the 2025 and 2026 budgets remained unused.

articles.title: Kitty Duterte to appeal Supreme Court ruling on father's ICC arrest
articles.summary: One of the children of detained former president Rodrigo Duterte will appeal the dismissal of the habeas corpus petition over his arrest and handover to the International Criminal Court.

blocks.text: November 25, 2026 | 4:00pm
Photos courtesy of the International Criminal Court show former president Rodrigo Duterte during his first in-person appearance before the tribunal since his arrest in March 2025.
Photos / ICC | via The STA / Janvic Mateo

MANILA, Philippines — One of the children of detained former president Rodrigo Duterte will appeal the dismissal of the habeas corpus petition over his arrest and handover to the International Criminal Court.
In a statement on Wednesday, November 25, Paolo Panelo, counsel for Duterte’s daughter Veronica "Kitty" Duterte, said that they would file a motion for reconsideration before the high court.

“Yesterday we received, with deep disappointment, the Supreme Court’s ruling dismissing the petitions for habeas corpus as moot, and declining to pass upon the legality of former President Rodrigo Duterte’s rendition to The Hague,” Panelo said.
“With due respect, the decision effectively reduces the great writ of habeas corpus to a race to remove the person detained outside Philippine territory before the courts can act,” he added.

Along with Veronica, his brothers, Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte and Rep. Paolo Duterte (Davao City 1st District), also filed habeas corpus petitions for their father on March 12, a day after the former president was handed over to the ICC.
The Supreme Court ruled that the petitions of the Duterte siblings are moot, as the former president is already under the jurisdiction of the ICC.
Improper joinder
Aside from dismissing the petitions, the Supreme Court said that there was an improper joinder of causes of action in the petition.
The high court, citing the rules of court, explained that “a joinder of causes of action shall not include special civil actions or actions governed by special procedural rules.”

“Taking cue from these legal and jurisprudential precepts, the Court is constrained to disallow the instant attempt to combine a petition for the issuance of a writ of habeas corpus with a petition for certiorari and/or prohibition,” the Supreme Court said.
“Since the former constitutes a special proceeding and the latter is classified as a special civil action, these two actions cannot be joined in a single pleading,” it added.

articles.title: Not all ferns are edible, DENR warns
articles.summary: The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) warned that not all "pako" or Philippine endemic ferns are safe to eat.

blocks.text: Published November 25, 2026 3:55pm
The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) warned that not all "pako" or Philippine endemic ferns are safe to eat.
There are around 12,000 fern species globally, with approximately 1,030 recorded in the Philippines, the department said.
The Lindsaea hamiguitanensis, which was first found and recorded in the Mt. Hamiguitan Range Wildlife Sanctuary in Davao Oriental, is not edible unlike the other Philippine endemic ferns.

"It is classified as Vulnerable under DENR Administrative Order No. 2026-20. Unlike edible pako varieties, there are limited studies on the edibility of this species. Thus, it is best not to forage, consume, or uproot it from the wild," the DENR Davao Region said.
The Lindsaea hamiguitanensis has relatively thin leaflets measuring approximately 1 to 1.8 centimeter long and 0.8 to 1 centimeter wide. They are also now found in other parts of Mindanao and Negros.
Moreover, the DENR said that pako plants are not only good for salads but also for the environment.

"Many ferns help prevent soil erosion, retain moisture on the forest floor, provide shelter for small organisms, and support nutrient recycling. These ecological functions play a vital role in maintaining healthy and resilient forest ecosystems," the DENR Davao Region said. — BAP, GMA News

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Trump did not praise Davao City’s energy security efforts
articles.summary: Reports from news outlets quoted the US leader saying, ‘We have more energy than any country in the world by double.’ The misleading posts misinterpret ‘double’ as ‘Davao.’

blocks.text: Claim: US President Donald Trump praised Davao City for its energy security efforts.

Why we fact-checked this: A Facebook reel bearing the claim was posted by the page Baste Duterte fan on November 21. The video has received 76,000 views, 1,700 reactions, 517 shares, and 139 comments as of writing.
The video shows Trump in a bilateral talk with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on November 18.

Text overlaid on the video reads, “[Number one] energy save security Davao City in the world.” The post further claimed that Marcos was supposedly taken aback when he heard Trump mention Davao City, the stronghold of his political rivals, the Dutertes.
Another Facebook reel, which has already garnered an estimated 704,000 views, also claimed that the US government will provide Davao City with a new energy project.

The facts: Nowhere in Trump’s statements during the bilateral talks did he say that Davao City was number one in the world for its energy security efforts. He also did not mention any new US government energy project for the city. No global rankings or news reports identify Davao City as a top city for energy conservation and security, contrary to the claim.

Reports from news outlets such as GMA News quoted Trump saying, “We have more energy than any country in the world by double.” The misleading post misinterpreted Trump’s pronunciation of “double” as “Davao.”

Trump was actually referring to US energy production. He claimed that the country is now the leading producer of oil and natural gas, surpassing the combined supply of Russia and Saudi Arabia, with the US leader also referencing its “acquisition” of Venezuela’s oil reserves. Trump also said the US aims to increase energy exports to Pacific allies, including the Philippines.

Trade deal: The posts circulated following Trump’s arrival in Manila on November 17 for a state visit and to participate in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations-US Special Summit, as well as the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue leaders’ summit.

During his visit, the US leader highlighted what he described as the “biggest trade deal” between the Philippines and the United States. The US is strengthening its defense partnership with the Philippines while signaling interest in expanding cooperation on energy security, particularly in nuclear energy.

US energy production: Trump’s remarks appeared to refer primarily to the United States’ energy production, particularly oil and natural gas. He has previously made the claim that the US is producing more oil and gas “than Russia and Saudi Arabia combined.” According to an article by PolitiFact, this remark is “mostly true,” but added that the US lead over the two countries “is built on the other liquids, not crude oil.”

According to Our World in Data, a project by UK-based nonprofit Global Change Data Lab, when considering total energy supply across different sources, including coal, oil, natural gas, renewables, and nuclear energy, China ranks first globally, with approximately 45,000 terawatt-hours in 2025.
Previous fact checks: Rappler has previously fact-checked similar false claims about Trump:

items: FACT CHECK: Trump did not call an ABS-CBN reporter ‘stupid’
FACT CHECK: Trump didn’t issue an arrest warrant against Marcos
FACT CHECK: No reports of Trump wanting to talk to Dela Rosa
FACT CHECK: No report of Trump courtesy call on Sara; Marcos remains president
FACT CHECK: No Trump plan to secure Duterte’s release from ICC

blocks.text: – Angelee Kaye Abelinde/Rappler.com
Angelee Kaye Abelinde is a student journalist based in Naga City, and an alumna of Rappler’s Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship 2024.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.summary: The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) on Wednesday has commissioned three vessels into service as part of efforts to bolster operational capabilities in protecting the country's maritime territories.

blocks.text: Published November 25, 2026 3:28pm
The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) on Wednesday has commissioned three vessels into service as part of efforts to bolster operational capabilities in protecting the country's maritime territories.

“The newly commissioned vessels will expand our conduct of maritime safety operations and responses to emergencies at sea, including oil spills and other incidents that threaten the country's rich marine environment,” PCG spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said in a statement.
The commissioning of the three vessels was held at the National Headquarters in Port Area, Manila led by PCG Commandant Admiral Rommel Supangan.
Two of the vessels, namely the BRP Patag (PATS-2701) and BRP Pag-asa (PATS-2702), are 27-meter marine protector-class patrol boats.
The boats came from the United States and were acquired after 24 PCG crew members completed specialized training in Baltimore, Maryland last August.
The third vessel is the BRP Kalikasan (MRSV-2001), a 20-meter marine research and survey vessel which will be used for shallow-water hydrographic surveys and ocean conservation.

The PCG said the BRP Kalikasan was built locally in Cebu as part of the PCG’s long-term capability expansion project. It was already used in a mission in Corregidor Island early this month. — BAP, GMA News

articles.title: Zimbabwe issues arrest warrant for Robert Mugabe's son over missed court date
articles.summary: The son of Zimbabwe's late former President Robert Mugabe has faced multiple legal troubles in the recent past.

blocks.text: A Zimbabwean court has issued an arrest warrant for Bellarmine Chatunga Mugabe, the youngest son of the country's late former president Robert Mugabe, after he failed to appear in court.
Mugabe was arrested earlier this month alongside four others over assault allegations on a police officer during an investigation into the suspected smuggling of luxury vehicles.
The group subsequently faced charges of robbery and malicious damage to property. They have yet to enter pleas.

They were granted bail on 6 November and were due back in court on Tuesday. However, Mugabe failed to attend. His co-accused, an aide and three security guards appeared and were remanded until 10 December.
Prosecutors allege that Mugabe and the others assaulted an investigating officer using their hands and broomsticks.
The officer's phone was allegedly taken and smashed on the ground, while one of the accused is said to have seized the officer's loaded pistol.
Bellarmine Chatunga is the youngest son of Robert Mugabe and his second wife, Grace Mugabe.
Robert Mugabe ruled Zimbabwe for 37 years before being forced from power in 2017, aged 93, following a military intervention. He died in 2019.
His son has attracted public attention in recent years over a series of legal troubles and his high-profile lifestyle.
Last month, he admitted to drug-related charges involving the possession of cannabis.

In April, he was deported from neighbouring South Africa after pleading guilty to pointing a firearm and being in the country illegally. He had been arrested following the shooting of a 23-year-old man at his home.
In 2023, he was arrested in Harare, Zimbabwe's capital, over allegations that he damaged property and spat at a police officer during a party.
He was later freed after reaching an out-of-court settlement with the complainant, who was a friend.

articles.title: Labor wins Greens support for trust changes in exchange for scrapping jet fuel subsidies for the wealthy
articles.summary: Government also agrees to carve out pensioners from cuts to private health insurance rebates in return for minor party’s support in Senate
articles.byline: Sarah Basford Canales and Krishani Dhanji

blocks.text: Private jet owners will no longer receive fuel tax subsidies after the Albanese government secured the Greens’ agreement to undo the sweetheart deal in exchange for supporting a controversial minimum tax rate on discretionary trusts.
The government is eager to pass four key pieces of legislation before parliament finishes for the year, including laws to create a gas reservation scheme.

The deal with the Greens to land discretionary trusts followed an earlier announcement that Labor had agreed to carve out pensioners from reductions to private health insurance rebates for over-65s in return for the minor party’s support in the upper house.
The Greens leader, David Shoebridge, said it was a “disgrace” that wealthier individuals with private aircraft only paid a fraction of the fuel excise to jet around the country.

“We can announce that we have forced the government to end the lurk where the ultra-wealthy are paying one-fifteenth of the tax on the fuel that they use to fill up their private jets [compared with] ordinary motorists,” he said.

“Whether it’s Gina Rinehart or Clive Palmer or Pauline Hanson, they’re now going to be paying the same effective rate when they fill up their tanks as ordinary Australians do in a cost-of-living crisis.”
The government excise applied to petrol used by specific aircrafts is below 4 cents a litre while petrol and diesel used in vehicles is 54 cents a litre.
The tax change will apply a minimum 30% tax rate on income received from discretionary trusts from 2029-30 and is estimated to raise $4.5bn in its first year of operation.
The opposition leader, Angus Taylor, accused the government of cutting a “dirty deal” with the Greens in a “war against small businesses”.
‘Realities of the Senate’
The Greens secured another major win early on Wednesday after the government agreed to carve out pensioners from its bill to decrease private health insurance rebates for over-65s.
The legislation, which had received public condemnation, was thrown out of the Senate last month by the Greens, Coalition and crossbench.
Shoebridge said the changes would stop 1.2 million pensioners from being forced to pay more.

“Around 2 million insured older Australians lived on less than $37,000 a year. These cuts would have left people going hungry or missing other essentials with no plan to reinvest in healthcare,” Shoebridge said.
after newsletter promotion
“At a time when the ultra-wealthy are making more and more, it was always wrong for Labor to even consider going after pensioners.”

Labor had promised the $3bn in savings from the budget measure would be spent on more aged care beds. The health minister, Mark Butler, said the government would fund the same amount, despite the carve out.
Butler acknowledged a deal was impossible without the major concession.

“The government also recognises the realities of the Senate, and reaching agreement was necessary to secure passage of the bill and deliver these important investments into aged care,” Butler said in a statement.

The digital duty of care passed on Wednesday afternoon with the Greens also backing it after negotiating for stronger penalties, including “multibillion-dollar” fines and allowing individuals to sue social media companies in court.
The week’s deals with the Greens to pass three pieces of legislation in the dying hours of the parliamentary year has left Labor with just one more hurdle – the gas reservation scheme.
The industry minister, Madeleine King, told News24 it was still the federal government’s intention to get the laws passed this week.
“Each senator will have to decide if they’re backing Aussie gas for Aussies,” King said.

articles.title: No funding for Pax Silica in BCDA's proposed 2027 budget
articles.summary: The Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) on Wednesday confirmed that there was no allocation for the proposed Pax Silica initiative under its proposed P1.14 billion national government…

blocks.text: Published November 25, 2026 3:16pm

The Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) on Wednesday confirmed that there was no allocation for the proposed Pax Silica initiative under its proposed P1.14 billion national government subsidy for fiscal year 2027.

Senator Bam Aquino, budget sponsor for BCDA, said this during the plenary deliberations when asked by Senator Imee Marcos about the allocation for Pax Silica under the proposed 2027 budget of the agency.
“There is none, Mr. President,” Aquino said.

Marcos pressed if the budget sponsor was categorically confirming that there was no allocation for Pax Silica under BCDA’s corporate operating budget for 2026 and 2027, including its internally generated funds.
“There is none. I'm confirming with our new President, Ariel Nepomuceno,” Aquino answered.
“There is no funding for Pax Silica in the GAA or with [BCDA’s] internally generated budget. So there is none,” he added.
Marcos then asked if there was any allocation for the compensation and relocation of residents expected to be displaced by the project.
Aquino said that P322 million in financial assistance was allocated, but clarified that the amount was not particularly for those affected by Pax Silica, but for all BCDA areas.
“But, if ever there would be assistance to the families there, it would be coming from this budget. It is not in the committee report; it is in their corporate funds,” he said.
No displacements?
During the plenary deliberations, the BCDA likewise committed to hold off on any possible displacement of residents due to the Pax Silica initiative, pending sufficient funds.

This came after Marcos asked who would be shouldering the cost that will be incurred by the transfer of those who will be possibly displaced, their relocation, and the restitution of their livelihoods if there was no corresponding budgetary allocation for Pax Silica.
“There’s a commitment that BCDA will be handling all of these concerns, while the locators will be funding the actual physical development of the area,” Aquino said.

Marcos clarified whether this means that the BCDA is committing that no resident will be displaced, no agricultural land will be cleared, and no community will be relocated until enough funds are secured and their rights are acknowledged and respected.
“Yes, there's a commitment, Mr. President, from BCDA,” Aquino answered. —AOL, GMA News

blocks.text: Six people, including two children, have been found dead after a plane crashed off the coast of Mississippi on Tuesday, the US Coast Guard says.

The Cessna 210 was on its way from New Orleans to Fort Myers, Florida, according to the flight tracking website FlightAware. Air traffic control lost touch with it at about 15:45 (21:45 GMT) and it later went down in the Gulf of Mexico between Pascagoula and Horn Island, officials said.
Divers found the bodies of four adults and two boys, aged 8 and 10, in the fuselage, said Coast Guard spokesperson Juan Ros.
Rescuers spent hours searching for the group and initially only found three life jackets, a life raft and the plane's cabin floating on the water, he said.

Cmdr Trevor Blount, the Coast Guard rescue mission co-ordinator, said: "While this is not the outcome any of us had hoped for, we are grateful for the strong interagency co-ordination that enabled us to swiftly locate those aboard the aircraft and provide closure to their families."

articles.title: AFP confirms Chinese bomber plane sighting 170 nautical miles from Manila
articles.summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Wednesday confirmed the sighting of a Chinese bomber plane near the shores of Luzon or 170 nautical miles away from Metro Manila.

blocks.text: Published November 25, 2026 2:58pm
The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Wednesday confirmed the sighting of a Chinese bomber plane near the shores of Luzon or 170 nautical miles away from Metro Manila.
AFP spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad was asked in a briefing regarding a Chinese H-6 strategic bomber reportedly seen in the West Philippine Sea.
Trinidad confirmed that the AFP monitored the plane.

“It only shows that the PLA (People's Liberation Army) … is now flexing its muscles. Sa baka dati-rati ang mga patrols niya were closer to the mainland of China. Today, mas umaabot sa atin,” Trinidad said during the Kapihan sa Manila Prince Hotel briefing.
(It only shows that the PLA (People's Liberation Army) … is now flexing its muscles. So before these patrols were closer to the mainland of China. Now, it is closer to us.)
“That bomber was 170 nautical miles from Metro Manila. The closest it got to our shorelines was, I think, 45 nautical miles,” he added.
GMA News Online sought comment from the Chinese Embassy and will publish it as soon as it is available.
Despite the bomber plane’s close proximity to the country, Trinidad said there was no reason for concern.
Trinidad said that there was no indication that the plane was practicing for a missile attack.

“It was a normal patrol conducted by the H-6 bomber. It has been conducted in the past over flights by bombers of the PLA Air Force over Scarborough Shoal, Bajo de Masinloc… There is no indicator that there was such a rehearsal for a missile strike,” Trinidad said.
Trinidad said that the AFP has already been able to modernize their capabilities to the point where they are able to monitor such aircraft before it enters the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone.

The Philippines and China have a longstanding row over the West Philippine Sea. Beijing has claimed most of the disputed waters for itself, despite the Permanent Court of Arbitration ruling that upheld Manila’s Exclusive Economic Zone.
China has consistently shown aggressive behavior in the disputed waters by blasting Philippine vessels with water cannons and tailing boats dangerously. —NB, GMA News

articles.title: Domestic violence soars to record high in Germany
articles.summary: Every three days in Germany, a man kills his wife or ex-partner. Every 10 minutes, the police record a sexual offense against a woman. "A shocking finding," according to Justice Minister Stefanie…

image.caption: Each November, the UN's Orange Day campaign highlights violence against womenImage: APA-Images/picture alliance

blocks.text: The German government has presented some grim statistics with regard to misogyny, rape, violence and murder, with reported cases of domestic violence at an all-time high.

At a press conference in Berlin on Tuesday, Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, Family Affairs Minister Karin Prien and Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig released the latest figures on crimes that specifically target women: whether within families and intimate relationships, in public or online.
'Behind all these terrible numbers lie individual stories'
In contrast to the statistics pertaining to crime overall, which have remained the same or increased only slightly, reports of crimes against women have increased.
"Behind all these terrible numbers lie individual stories, people and particularly women and girls, whose lives are severely affected by these acts of violence," said Dobrindt.
Behind domestic violence: Causes, patterns and solutions

In 2025, some 280,000 people were victims of physical abuse in their own homes, a 2.8% increase compared to the previous year. Over 70% of the victims were female. Each hour, 16 women are subjected to physical abuse behind closed doors.
The male victims included boys who had been assaulted by their fathers.
The number of misogynistic hate crimes has also risen dramatically, by almost 50%, to 819 cases.

"The figures show us what it can mean to be a woman in Germany," said Hubig. "It can mean being killed by one's partner or ex-partner. Being a woman can also mean being physically abused by one's partner or ex-partner in one's own home. Being a woman can mean that one's sexual autonomy is brutally disregarded."
Perpetrators, victims getting younger

According to the latest findings, both perpetrators and victims are getting younger. In 2025, nearly half of all female victims of sexual offenses were under the age of 18. And the number of incidents of online violence against women and girls rose by 15.7%. This includes the unauthorized sharing of videos and photos, verbal abuse, manipulation of images, threats and online blackmail, as well as cyberstalking.

Because many perpetrators and victims are still in their teens, Prien, who is also minister for education, said the government wanted to focus primarily on schools, which she explained should become places of prevention.
"Ultimately, we need to bring about a change in people's mindsets, especially those of men. That will be the deciding factor in the end," she said.
Femicides to be classified as murder, not manslaughter

Over the weekend, Justice Minister Hubig had already announced that in future all femicides, the intentional killing of girls and women because of their gender, would be classified as murders. Currently, such crimes are often classified as manslaughter, for which the penalty is less severe than for murder.
Hubig told German broadcaster ZDF that it was increasingly common that femicides be described as family tragedies or as domestic dramas revolving around jealousy and then classified as manslaughter.

Martina Link, the vice president of the Federal Criminal Police Office, was also at the press conference in Berlin. She called for everybody to pay closer attention to the issue, within their own families, neighborhoods or at work.
"Violence against women is not a private matter," she said. "Not in our immediate surroundings nor in the digital world."
She also pointed out that when it came to sexual offenses and domestic violence, only about 5-10% of cases were reported.
This article was originally written in German.
Why women say politics is becoming more hostile

articles.title: Number of Pinoy families who consider themselves poor unchanged — OCTA
articles.summary: About 9.8 million Filipino families considered themselves poor in October 2026, noting that self-rated poverty remained statistically unchanged from the firm's previous findings in July 2026.

blocks.text: November 25, 2026 | 2:37pm
Children sorting through garbage at a slums along the shoreline of Baseco Beach in Manila on Sept. 28, 2019.
AFP / Maria Tan

MANILA, Philippines — Private polling firm OCTA Research reported that about 9.8 million Filipino families considered themselves poor in October 2026, noting that self-rated poverty remained statistically unchanged from the firm's previous findings in July 2026.
Although the nominal figures for October were lower than the previous quarter's rates, the firm said that the differences should not be interpreted as declines.
The firm said that the differences fell within the survey's margin of error of ±3 percentage points, meaning that there were no significant differences between the data sets.
Self-rated poverty stood at 37% in OCTA's Tugon ng Masa results for the third quarter of 2026.
Mindanao had the highest rate of self-reported poverty at 56%, followed by the Visayas at 49%. The median amount reported as lacking among families identifying as poor was around P5,000.
Self-rated hunger, meanwhile, was reported at 22%, well above the 17% recorded in March 2026.

Low- to very-low-income families were particularly affected, with 49% reporting that they had experienced hunger. Across major areas, self-rated hunger was most prevalent in the National Capital Region and the Visayas, at 29% each.
However, food poverty, which refers to the struggle to obtain sufficient food, was highest in Mindanao at 54%.
Among socioeconomic classes, low- to very-low-income households similarly reported the highest food poverty rate, underlining their continued vulnerability to food hardship.
Overall food inflation eased slightly to 6.4% from 6.8% in October 2026, but faster increases were still seen in the prices of rice and corn.
Combined, the crops have accounted for more than 92% of agricultural losses attributed to the Super El Niño so far.
These and other damages will be reflected in the Philippine Statistics Authority's November 2026 inflation data, scheduled for release on December 4.

articles.title: Four years after huge asteroid crash, a spacecraft has now returned to assess the damage
articles.summary: The mission is studying an asteroid deliberately knocked off course by a colliding spacecraft.
articles.byline: Rebecca Morelle, Alison Francis, Tony Jolliffe

blocks.text: Four years after huge asteroid crash, a spacecraft has now returned to assess the damage
Image source, ESA
The Hera spacecraft will study the 150m-wide (490ft) asteroid called Dimorphos
A spacecraft has arrived at an asteroid to investigate the damage caused by an unprecedented cosmic crash.
It what may sound like the plot of a disaster movie, Nasa's Dart spacecraft deliberately smashed into the space rock in 2022 to knock it off course.

The Nasa craft was obliterated on impact. Four years on, a European Space Agency (ESA) mission, called Hera, is scouring the scene to fully assess the aftermath of the collision - with the first images set to be released later on Wednesday.
The asteroid poses no threat, instead this was the first ever test of our planetary defences to see what action we could take if a space rock was heading for our planet.
"Hera is a sort of Inspector Columbo going back to the crash scene to investigate what is the outcome of this impact," said Patrick Michel, principal investigator of ESA's Hera mission.

blocks.caption: Image caption, This was the last image from Dart before it crashed into Dimorphos in 2022

blocks.text: Image source, NASA/Johns Hopkins APL
This was the last image from Dart before it crashed into Dimorphos in 2022
The crash test focussed on a pair of asteroids: a larger one called Didymos - about 730m (2,400ft) wide - which is orbited by a smaller rock called Dimorphos, about 150m (490ft) wide.

The Dart spacecraft targeted Dimorphos, hurtling into the rock at 22,000km per hour (14,000mph). Images beamed back showed the asteroid's rocky surface coming ever closer until the feed cut out on impact.
It was such a big smash-up that the trail of debris, measuring about 10,000km long (6,200 miles), was spotted by telescopes on Earth and in space.
The crash showed it was possible to change the path of the smaller asteroid.
Before the collision it took Dimorphos 11 hours and 55 minutes to orbit around Didymos. After the Dart crash, the duration of its orbit had shrunk by about 33 minutes.
But the arrival of the second spacecraft, Hera, will help scientists to answer many more questions.
"Dart exploded in the asteroid, and therefore we don't have the information of what is its final state," explained Michel.
"The impact could have left a crater - and if it is the case, we need to understand the size and the depth. Or [the impact] may have entirely reshaped the asteroid."

blocks.caption: Image caption, A 10,000km-long (6,200 miles) debris trail was spotted by the Hubble Space Telescope

blocks.text: Image source, NASA/Hubble Space Telescope
A 10,000km-long (6,200 miles) debris trail was spotted by the Hubble Space Telescope
The Hera mission will spend the next year studying Dimorphos, and take a look at Didymos too.
The spacecraft is packed with instruments, and it also has two small shoe-boxed sized satellites onboard, which can study the impact site up close, and then later land on the asteroid.
A key task is to measure the mass of Dimorphos, to work out how effective the spacecraft's shove was.
This information would be vital if we ever spotted a space rock that was on a collision course with Earth.
"It would help us to predict what would happen if we had to hit another asteroid," said Prof Simon Green, a planetary scientist who is on Hera's science team.
"We [could] measure its properties and say: 'Well, we need this mass of spacecraft, travelling at this speed, this early, in order to deflect it enough so that it misses the Earth'."

blocks.caption: Image caption, Hera has already sent back an image of Didymos with Dimorphos in the background

blocks.text: Hera has already sent back an image of Didymos with Dimorphos in the background
Asteroids pose a significant threat to our planet.
The biggest, which measure more than a kilometre across, could cause global devastation. But medium-sized asteroids around the same dimensions as Dimorphos could wipe out a city.

"We all know what happened to the dinosaurs, right? And we don't want that to happen to us," said Carolyn Ernst, Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory, who works on both the Dart and Hera missions.
"The good news for us is that there are far fewer potential threats out there in the Solar System than there were millions of years ago. But there are objects out there."
She said the biggest asteroids have been spotted, and none are heading to Earth.
"The smallest stuff isn't too much of a threat because our atmosphere protects us," she added.

"But there's a size range in the middle where we don't know where all of them are, and it could, if impacted, cause problems for humanity. And if we can find out about that and know about that, well, we sure as heck would want to try to stop that."

blocks.caption: Image caption, Hera has two small satellites onboard to study the asteroid up close

blocks.text: Hera has two small satellites onboard to study the asteroid up close
Scientists want to gather as much intelligence as they can about space rocks - to make us as well equipped as possible to deal with whatever the Universe throws at us.
A new mission is launching in 2027 to track potentially hazardous asteroids: a space telescope called the Near-Earth Object (NEO) Surveyor.
There are also more visits planned to asteroids, including to one called Apophis, which is about 450m (1,480ft) long.
Apophis was discovered in 2004 and it was initially thought it might hit the Earth as early as 13 April 2029.
But now scientists understand its orbit better, and say it won't hit us for at least the next 100 years. Instead of a crash in 2029, it will fly just 32,000km (20,000 miles) above our surface.
This will give scientists the rare chance to study a space rock up-close.

Two spacecraft will head to Apophis, including Nasa's Osiris-Apex (which previously grabbed a sample from another asteroid called Bennu) and Ramses, a joint mission between ESA and the Japanese Space Agency (JAXA).

articles.title: Francis called Tagle ‘a saint’ and ‘kindness incarnate,’ book on late pope’s diary says
articles.summary: Pope Francis once described Luis Antonio Cardinal Tagle as “a saint who possesses the best of Asian qualities—kindness incarnate,” according to a new book by one of the late…

blocks.text: November 25, 2026 | 1:32pm

MANILA, Philippines — Pope Francis once described Luis Antonio Cardinal Tagle as “a saint who possesses the best of Asian qualities—kindness incarnate,” according to a new book by one of the late pontiff’s closest confidantes that draws on a diary Francis kept for more than three decades.
Cardinal Víctor Manuel “Tucho” Fernández, who compiled and annotated "The Private Diary of Pope Francis," recalls the remark from his own conversations with the late pontiff.
He cites it as an example of how the pope spoke well of his collaborators in the Roman Curia “even when someone tried to provoke him into expressing criticism.”
The 160-page book was released on Tuesday, November 24, in five languages and 94 countries by the Vatican Publishing House. Pope Francis died at age 88 on April 21, 2025.
In the same passage, Fernández, who heads the Vatican’s Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith, recalls Francis’s praise for four other senior churchmen.

The late pope said Cardinal Robert Prevost — now Pope Leo XIV, whom he brought to Rome in 2023 to lead the office that vets bishop appointments — had always been “a great pastor, a generous missionary, and an irreproachable man.”
Francis also called Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican secretary of state, “an excellent diplomat, the cardinal who best understood international politics.”

Francis also spoke well of two cardinals widely seen as critics of his papacy. He described Guinea’s Cardinal Robert Sarah as a believer “with a refined spiritual sensitivity” and said Germany’s Cardinal Gerhard Müller “seems aggressive, but he’s a good man, but good, good.”
Francis had declined to renew Müller’s term as the Vatican’s doctrine chief in 2017 and accepted Sarah’s resignation as head of its worship office in 2021.
Dean of the cardinals
Tagle was himself viewed as part of the inner circle of the late Pope Francis and had worked closely with him for most of his 12-year papacy.
As archbishop of Manila, Tagle hosted the Francis' January 2015 visit, when 6 million to 7 million people attended the closing Mass at Rizal Park, a record for a papal event.
Francis brought Tagle to Rome in 2019 to lead the Vatican’s missionary office, and in 2022 named him pro-prefect of its section for first evangelization, the post he still holds under Pope Leo.
Tagle is also dean of the College of Cardinals, a position he was elected to in October, making him the first Asian prelate to hold the post.
Often dubbed in Catholic media as the “Asian Francis,” Tagle was among the most discussed contenders to succeed Francis before the May 2025 conclave, which elected Prevost.
Pope Francis kept long-term diary
Francis wrote intermittently in a black-covered planner for the year 1992 that he never used for appointments, according to Fernández.
The entries run from Dec. 20, 1992 — the year he was named auxiliary bishop of Buenos Aires — to Aug. 18, 2024, eight months before his death.
In all, Francis filled 86 pages before his 2013 election and 55 as pope.
The most confidential matters are written in code, “using symbols that we cannot and should not decipher,” Fernández writes.
He says he also left out details that directly affect third parties and, in some cases, names.
Fernández says Francis showed him the notebook at the Casa Santa Marta, the Vatican guesthouse where the pope lived, telling him: “From this, you will all see.”
A few weeks after Leo’s election, Fernández told the new pope he feared the writings “might end up abandoned in a warehouse somewhere.” Leo sent him the cardboard box of papers days later.
Fernández writes that he ultimately spent a year preparing the book.
Crisis and ‘the entrance to hell’
International media outlets have widely focused on Francis’s account of his own spiritual struggles as detailed in his diary.

According to the book, the Argentine pope went through a crisis from January 2021 to December 2022, as his health worsened, connected to what he saw as a temptation to exercise power over others. In a December 2022 entry, he described it as “all mixed with governance issues, pressure regarding decisions to make, and aridity and desolation.”

He also wrote that he believed he had seen the devil three times, once during a meeting after returning to Rome. In an entry dated June 7, 2018, as the scale of the clergy sexual abuse scandal in Chile became clear to him, he wrote: “Last night I saw the entrance to hell.” He added that he “grabbed the Rosary as a weapon.”

Fernández cautions against reading this as proof that Francis was manipulative. “It is not easy to find an important event that took place between 2021 and 2022 in which he outwardly manifested what he so deeply regretted,” he writes, calling the experience “more internal than external.”
‘Like a delicate crystal’

The remarks about Tagle, Prevost, Parolin and other cardinals appear in a chapter on what Fernández calls Francis’s “unshakable” conviction about human dignity, or the belief that every person “must be treated like a delicate crystal.”
Fernández writes that during meetings or meals, Francis was “evidently upset if someone present treated an employee impolitely or spoke to another person sarcastically.”

Elsewhere, Fernández recounts that Francis grew fond of an immigrant woman who worked at Santa Marta. One morning he was told she had died suddenly. Minutes later, a visiting president arrived, and some media outlets read the pope’s downcast face as a sign of disrespect.
Fernández also writes that he once told Francis he was “quite hard of hearing” and asked how he answered questions he had not fully heard.
“My intuition saves me,” the pope replied, according to Fernández.
That intuition, Fernández says, explains why Francis “would sometimes say one thing and in other contexts seem to say something different” — a complaint long raised by his critics.
Popular piety
The book also takes up a subject close to Filipino Catholics: Francis’s regard for popular piety, the devotions and traditions ordinary believers practice outside formal liturgy.

Fernández writes that during his years as a bishop in Latin America, Francis drew on the document produced by the region’s bishops at Puebla, Mexico, in 1979, which treated popular religion as an expression of a people’s culture.
In his personal copy, Francis underlined passages on “the new valuation of popular religiosity” but not a phrase referring to its “distortions and ambiguities.”
“He was tired of the criticism directed at popular piety coming from certain sectors, both traditionalists and progressives,” Fernández writes.
In the Philippines, such devotions draw millions every year, among them the Traslacion of the Black Nazarene in Manila and the Sinulog festival in Cebu honoring the Santo Niño.

Francis tied the Santo Niño to Filipino family life in a video message for the 500th anniversary of Christianity in the country, released by the Vatican on April 4, 2021. Francis said the image of the Holy Child, “a symbol of the arrival of Christianity in your archipelago,” recalls the hidden life of the Holy Family in Nazareth. — With reports by Ian Laqui
